# Results — Study 646 (BoJ Announcement Effect)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — **Japanese
equities and the yen react systematically to Bank of Japan policy decision days**, especially
in the "surprise" NIRP (2016) / YCC-tweak (2016, 2022-24) eras. Offline & deterministic once
cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the
last complete calendar month; the partial current month is dropped). Fingerprints
`e6d94e03a855` (EWJ) / `70f450fc971e` (JPY=X).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily EWJ raw OHLC (5,406 rows) + `JPY=X` (USDJPY) OHLC (5,574 rows), 2005-01-03 → 2026-06-30 |
| BoJ decision calendar | **hardcoded** table of **248 decision/statement dates** 2005-01-19 → 2026-06-16 (Bank of Japan official archives — every decision on record, scheduled AND the rare inter-meeting/emergency ones; the claim under test is explicitly about the surprise-driven eras, so nothing is filtered out) |
| Events | **247** of 248 decision days sit on the EWJ tape (1 missing: **2012-10-30**, NYSE closed for Hurricane Sandy), vs **5,157** other trading days |
| Statistics | Welch *t* for the group splits; **Newey-West (5 lags)** *t* on the decision-day dummy regression as the serial-correlation-robust cross-check; Wilson interval on the hit rate; 20-seed × 1,000-draw random-calendar placebo (two-sided — BoJ surprises have no pre-committed sign) |
| Execution / lag | one documented convention: the BoJ statement hits the tape during the Tokyo morning session on decision day D. EWJ's US-session close on date D sits after Tokyo's full reaction — zero look-ahead. **Yen return is dated D as Open[D+1]/Open[D] − 1** (see the data quirk below), a window that still starts before the ~11:30am JST announcement |
| Third axis (tradability) | hold the instrument for the decision day only, entered at the **prior close** (the BoJ's yearly meeting schedule is published in advance — zero look-ahead) and exited at the decision-day close/next-open leg; one round trip = 2 × one-way cost × NAV; long-only, no borrow |
| Data quirk (named) | From 2022 onward, yfinance's `JPY=X` daily bars have `Close` silently **duplicate the same row's Open** on >95% of days (verified; <5% pre-2022) — a Yahoo FX-data limitation, not a study artifact. It would mute/mistime exactly the tail events this study cares about (the Dec-2022 shock reads as flat under the broken field), so the yen return uses `Open[D+1]/Open[D]` uniformly across the **whole** 2005-2026 sample instead — one convention, no era-dependent switch. `High`/`Low` remain reliable throughout, so realized range uses `(High−Low)/Open` |

No survivorship on the Signal axis: EWJ and `JPY=X` are a fund and an FX rate, not a
survivor-conditioned basket.

## The headline — BoJ decision-day return vs all other days

EWJ = unhedged Japan equities (USD); yen return = **minus** the USDJPY change (positive = yen
strengthens — same sign convention as sibling study
[615-yen-safe-haven](../../615-yen-safe-haven/)).

| quantity | EWJ | yen |
|---|--:|--:|
| decision-day mean return | +0.0080% | −0.0633% |
| other-day mean return | +0.0145% | −0.0058% |
| gap | −0.0065% | −0.0575% |
| Welch *t* | **−0.06** | **−0.85** |
| Newey-West *t* (5 lags) | −0.06 | −0.85 |
| hit rate (return > 0) | 118/247 = **47.8%** (Wilson [41.6%, 54.0%]) | 117/247 = **47.4%** (Wilson [41.2%, 53.6%]) |

Neither instrument clears the desk bar (**\|t\| ≥ 2**) by any margin — both sit well inside
coin-flip territory, and both hit rates sit *below* 50%. **Random-calendar placebo (two-sided,
20,000 draws):** EWJ observed +0.0080% vs placebo mean +0.0147% (sd 0.0788%) → **p = 0.9223**;
yen observed −0.0633% vs placebo mean −0.0057% (sd 0.0453%) → **p = 0.1584**. A random calendar
of 247 days reproduces the observed gap the large majority of the time on both instruments.

## Event window — build-up and persistence (mean return %, Welch *t* vs far-from-meeting days)

| offset | −5 | −4 | −3 | −2 | −1 | **0** | +1 | +2 | +3 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| EWJ mean % | −0.127 | −0.072 | +0.016 | −0.104 | +0.105 | **+0.040** | +0.013 | −0.011 | −0.004 |
| EWJ Welch *t* | −1.76 | −1.40 | −0.19 | −1.51 | +0.69 | **+0.04** | −0.23 | −0.49 | −0.49 |
| yen mean % | +0.026 | +0.036 | −0.058 | −0.051 | +0.007 | **−0.042** | +0.036 | −0.026 | −0.077 |
| yen Welch *t* | +0.52 | +0.68 | −1.19 | −1.02 | +0.21 | **−0.65** | +0.98 | −0.51 | −0.88 |

No offset in the [−5..+3] window — including the decision day itself — reaches the desk bar
for either instrument. There is no build-up, no decision-day spike, and no persistence to
detect: the whole window looks like sampling noise around zero.

## Realized range on the same days — the grey third-axis myth-check

"Do BoJ decision days swing MORE than an average day, regardless of direction?" (H−L)/day-open.

| metric | BoJ days | other days | Welch *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| EWJ range | **1.164%** | 0.995% | **+2.49** |
| yen range | **1.059%** | 0.760% | **+6.30** |

Both clear the desk bar. Unlike the direction, the **amplitude** is genuinely elevated on BoJ
days — a decision day is a materially louder day for both Japanese equities and the yen, even
though the average sign of that extra motion cancels out across 247 events.

## Era contrast — pre-NIRP/YCC vs the "surprise regime" (split 2016-01-29, justified: the NIRP announcement itself)

| era | EWJ decision-day mean | *n* | within-era Welch *t* | yen decision-day mean | *n* | within-era Welch *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2005 → 2016-01-28 | −0.001% | 162 | −0.02 | −0.100% | 162 | −1.19 |
| 2016-01-29 → 2026 | +0.025% | 85 | −0.02 | +0.006% | 85 | +0.16 |
| Welch *t* of the difference | | | **+0.13** | | | **+0.75** |

Neither era, nor the difference between them, reaches the desk bar. The NIRP/YCC "surprise
regime" is not, on average, more directionally reactive than the earlier near-zero-rate era —
consistent with the tail-event reading below: the era contains genuine surprises, but they cut
in *both* directions and cancel on average.

## Named surprise tail events — illustrative only, never used to certify the average-day stamp

z-scores vs the 247-event BoJ-day distribution.

| date | event | EWJ | EWJ *z* | yen | yen *z* | EWJ range | yen range |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2016-01-29 | NIRP announced | +2.38% | +1.41 | −2.01% | −1.86 | 1.87% | 2.64% |
| 2016-09-21 | YCC introduced | +2.88% | +1.71 | +1.18% | +1.19 | 1.14% | 2.18% |
| 2022-12-20 | YCC band widened ("Kuroda shock") | +1.41% | +0.84 | **+3.80%** | **+3.69** | 1.29% | **4.70%** |
| 2023-07-28 | YCC made more flexible | +0.57% | +0.33 | −1.35% | −1.23 | 0.62% | 2.06% |
| 2023-10-31 | YCC further loosened | +1.21% | +0.72 | −1.45% | −1.33 | 0.84% | 1.68% |
| 2024-03-19 | NIRP/YCC formally ended | +0.38% | +0.22 | −1.26% | −1.14 | 0.79% | 1.15% |
| 2024-07-31 | Rate hike to ~0.25% (pre-carry-unwind) | +2.90% | +1.72 | +1.94% | +1.91 | 0.99% | 2.57% |

This is the honest anatomy of "surprise-driven, not scheduled-directional": EWJ is
**positive on every single one of these seven headline surprises** (a hawkish AND a dovish
surprise both, historically, coincided with Japanese equities *rallying* — a relief-rally
pattern, not a directional edge you could have called ex ante), while the yen **swings both
ways depending on whether the surprise was read as hawkish or dovish relative to what was
priced in** (weakens on the dovish NIRP/YCC-loosening days, strengthens sharply on the hawkish
band-widening/hike days). Only the Dec-2022 "Kuroda shock" individually clears \|z\| ≥ 2 on any
metric (yen *z* = +3.69) — a single tail event, not a repeatable pattern.

## Third axis — tradability: hold the decision day only, enter prior close, exit decision close

BoJ's yearly meeting schedule is published in advance — zero look-ahead scheduled entry; one
round trip = 2 × one-way cost × NAV; long-only, no borrow.

| quantity | EWJ | yen |
|---|--:|--:|
| gross per event | +0.80 bps | −6.33 bps |
| net per event (5 / 10 bps one-way) | **−9.20 / −19.20 bps** | **−16.33 / −26.33 bps** |
| all-other-days mean | +1.45 bps | −0.58 bps |
| Welch *t* (BoJ vs other days) | −0.06 | −0.85 |
| hit rate | 47.8% | 47.4% |
| worst single decision day | **−8.06%** | **−7.80%** |
| best single decision day | +5.97% | +3.80% |

Gross is already indistinguishable from zero on both legs; costs alone turn it decisively
negative. Neither instrument offers anything to harvest — and both carry an **8%-scale tail**
on the wrong day (the March-2011 post-earthquake session and the 2008/2020 crisis clusters sit
in these worst-day figures).

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic i.i.d.-return world with scheduled pseudo-decision days every 12th business day
and a TUNABLE planted mean shift; no network.

| world | Welch *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (effect = 0), **20 seeds** | mean **−0.23** (sd 1.34), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 3/20 seeds** |
| planted effect = +0.20% (seed 646) | **+5.46** |

A 100-seed check gives an empirical false-positive rate of **3%**, consistent with the nominal
~5% for a single test — the 3/20 in the canonical 20-seed run is ordinary sampling noise, not a
biased detector. The detector recovers a planted shift far smaller than the tail events above
(+0.20% vs the ~2-4% surprise-day moves). *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited
in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Neither EWJ (Welch *t* = −0.06) nor the yen (Welch *t* = −0.85) shows a
  systematic decision-day reaction across 247 BoJ decisions 2005-2026: both hit rates sit
  *below* 50%, both random-calendar placebos are unremarkable (*p* = 0.92, 0.16), and no
  offset in the [−5..+3] event window reaches the desk bar. The NIRP/YCC "surprise regime"
  split doesn't rescue it either (diff *t* = +0.13 / +0.75) — surprises happened, but they cut
  both directions and cancel on average.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** With no average edge to harvest, costs alone turn both legs
  decisively negative (EWJ −9.2/−19.2 bps net, yen −16.3/−26.3 bps net at 5/10 bps), and both
  carry an 8%-scale worst-day tail.
- **"BoJ days swing MORE than an average day"? — CONFIRMED.** Realized range is elevated on
  both EWJ (Welch *t* = +2.49) and the yen (Welch *t* = +6.30) — decision days are genuinely
  louder, even though the *direction* of that extra motion is unpredictable. The one hand-
  picked tail event that clears \|z\| ≥ 2 individually (Dec-2022 "Kuroda shock", yen *z* =
  +3.69) illustrates exactly this: real, occasionally huge, but not a repeatable calendar
  effect.
